drugRefs.regimenLabel: Per prior sputum culture if available; empirically Amoxicillin-clavulanate if no Pseudomonas history
drugRefs.why: Bronchiectasis exacerbations are typically treated with longer courses than simple bronchitis given the structural lung disease; prior culture history should directly guide empiric choice given high rates of chronic colonization.
First-line oral option with reliable antipseudomonal activity for patients with known Pseudomonas colonization, avoiding the need for IV therapy in milder exacerbations.

drugRefs.coverage: Used for more severe exacerbations or treatment failure on oral antipseudomonal therapy.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Choice must be tailored to known colonization status — a one-size-fits-all empiric regimen is not appropriate for bronchiectasis.
gaps: Empiric therapy without checking prior culture history risks under-treating chronic Pseudomonas colonization.

stewardship.deescalation: Narrow to the most targeted oral agent once current sputum culture results are available, and ensure the patient's chronic colonization record is updated for future exacerbations.

drugs.drug: Per prior sputum culture if available; empirically Amoxicillin-clavulanate if no Pseudomonas history
drugs.why: Bronchiectasis exacerbations are typically treated with longer courses than simple bronchitis given the structural lung disease; prior culture history should directly guide empiric choice given high rates of chronic colonization.
First-line oral option with reliable antipseudomonal activity for patients with known Pseudomonas colonization, avoiding the need for IV therapy in milder exacerbations.

drugs.coverage: Used for more severe exacerbations or treatment failure on oral antipseudomonal therapy.

framework: Always check prior sputum culture history before choosing empiric therapy — this is the single most important stewardship action in bronchiectasis exacerbations given individual colonization patterns.
Longer courses (10-14 days) are appropriate for bronchiectasis exacerbations, unlike the shorter courses used for simple bronchitis, given the structural lung disease.
Address airway clearance (chest physiotherapy, mucolytics) as a critical adjunct to antibiotics, not optional.
